summary.text: LaToya Nkongolo is a Republican member of the Maryland House of Delegates from District 31, in Anne Arundel County, and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A social worker and behavioral health business owner, she has served in the House since January 2025 and sits on the Judiciary Committee.

paragraphs.text: Nkongolo was born in Wilmington, Delaware.

She earned a bachelor's degree in social work from Delaware State University in 2000, a master's degree in organizational management and leadership from Springfield College in 2003, and a master of social work degree from the University of Maryland, Baltimore in 2013.

She worked as a family program supervisor at Anne Arundel Medical Center, deputy executive director of Nick's Place, and program manager for recovery support services at the Anne Arundel County Department of Health, has taught as an adjunct professor at Anne Arundel Community College since 2015, and has owned Work Life Behavioral Health and Professional Training, LLC since 2016.
Gov. Wes Moore appointed Nkongolo to the House of Delegates on January 3, 2025, to replace Rachel Muñoz, and she has served since January 10, 2025.
She sits on the Judiciary Committee and its Civil, Criminal, and Estates and Trusts subcommittees, and has been a Deputy Minority Whip in 2026.
